## Function Validate Card

Turns an untrusted object into a Card or a list of faults.

Behaviour: Required: customId matching ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$ and not ending in .r<digits> (/\.r[0-9]+$/: the suffix of its own retry id; fault "customId '<id>' ends in .r<n>, the suffix of a retry"), intent generate|patch, targets a non-empty list of distinct repo-relative paths (normalised: not "", ".", "..", absolute or under "../"), instruction a non-empty string. Optional with defaults: contextSlice [] (empty means "no context, instruction only" — never the whole project), acceptance null, model null, maxTokens null, reasoning null, variants 1, dependsOn []. Unknown keys are faults, never ignored. Every fault names the key and the rule in one line; all faults are reported at once.

Steps:
- produces: Card

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given {"customId":"a","intent":"generate","targets":["src/a.ts"],"instruction":"x"}; when validated; then a Card with contextSlice [], variants 1, dependsOn [], acceptance null
2. given {"customId":"bad id","intent":"generate","targets":["src/a.ts"],"instruction":"x"}; when validated; then one fault: customId 'bad id' does not match ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$
3. given {"customId":"a","intent":"todo","targets":[],"instruction":""}; when validated; then exactly three faults, in key order: intent, targets, instruction
4. given {"customId":"a","intent":"generate","targets":["src/a.ts","./src/a.ts"],"instruction":"x"}; when validated; then one fault: targets repeat src/a.ts after normalisation
5. given {"customId":"lint.r2","intent":"generate","targets":["src/a.ts"],"instruction":"x"}; when validated; then one fault: customId 'lint.r2' ends in .r<n>, the suffix of a retry

## Function Load Deck

Reads a deck file (a JSON array of cards) into a Deck.

Behaviour: Every element is validated with Validate Card; duplicate customIds and a dependsOn cycle are deck faults; a dependsOn naming a card outside the deck is external and allowed. The Deck keeps file order.

Steps:
- calls: Validate Card
- reads: Deck File
- produces: Deck

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given a file with cards a, b, b; when loaded; then one deck fault: duplicate customId b

## Function Commit Paths

Stages exactly the given paths and commits them with a subject and trailers; null when nothing changed.

Behaviour: commitPaths(root, paths, subject, trailers, env, force = false): `git add -A -- <paths>` (`git add -A -f -- <paths>` when force); `git diff --cached --name-only -- <paths>` empty → null, no commit. Else `git commit -q -m <subject> -m <trailer block> -- <paths>`, the trailer block being one "<key>: <value>" line per trailer in the given order joined by "\n" (hooks run; nothing is bypassed), so the message is "<subject>\n\n<trailer lines>". Only the paths are committed: a file staged by hand or modified outside them stays as it was. Then commit = `git rev-parse HEAD` (trimmed) and the diffstat from `git show --numstat --format= <commit>`: files = the number of non-empty lines, insertions and deletions the sums of the first two columns ("-" for a binary file counts 0). Returns Commit Info.

Steps:
- calls: Run Git
- produces: Commit Info

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given a fresh repo; other.txt written and staged by hand (git add other.txt); notes.txt untracked; src/a.ts written "export const a = 1;\n"; paths ["src/a.ts"], subject "s", trailers [["K", "v"]]; when committed; then Commit Info {commit: HEAD (40 hex), diffstat {files: 1, insertions: 1, deletions: 0}}; the HEAD message is "s\n\nK: v"; `git show --name-only --format= HEAD` lists only src/a.ts; other.txt is still staged (`git diff --cached --name-only` reads "other.txt") and notes.txt still untracked
2. given a repo where src/a.ts is committed with "export const a = 1;\n" and is unchanged; paths ["src/a.ts"]; when committed; then null; HEAD is the commit it was before

Data Commit Info: One commit and what it changed; structurally runloop's CommitInfo, so makeCommitHook is a CommitHook.
Schema:
{ commit: string, diffstat: { files: number, insertions: number, deletions: number } }

## Function Commit Card

Stages exactly the card's targets; subject 'morph <id>: <targets>'; trailers Morph-Card, Morph-Model, Morph-Variant (if given), Morph-Acceptance-Exit; returns sha and diffstat, or null when nothing changed. makeCommitHook binds it into runloop's commit hook.

Behaviour: commitCard(root, {customId, targets, model, variant, acceptanceExit}, env) is Commit Paths over targets with force true (a target under a .gitignore'd path is committed: the card named it, so its hook never throws on it) and subject "morph <customId>: <targets joined by ", ">" and trailers Morph-Card <customId>, Morph-Model <model>, Morph-Variant <variant> only when variant is not null, Morph-Acceptance-Exit <acceptanceExit>, in that order. makeCommitHook(root, model, env) returns (customId, targets) => commitCard(root, {customId, targets, model, variant: null, acceptanceExit: 0}, env): runloop fires its hook only for an accepted card (exit 0) and does not pass the winning variant, so the hook writes no Morph-Variant.

Steps:
- calls: Commit Paths
- produces: Commit Info

Examples (the tests must prove each one):

2. given a repo where src/a.ts is committed with "export const a = 1;\n"; then src/a.ts rewritten "export const a = 2;\nexport const z = 0;\n"; customId "c", targets ["src/a.ts"], model "glm53", variant "c.v2", acceptanceExit 0; when committed; then diffstat {files: 1, insertions: 2, deletions: 1}; the HEAD message is "morph c: src/a.ts\n\nMorph-Card: c\nMorph-Model: glm53\nMorph-Variant: c.v2\nMorph-Acceptance-Exit: 0"
3. given a fresh repo; hook = makeCommitHook(root, "stub", env); out/h.ts written "x\n"; then the hook called again with nothing changed; when hook("h", ["out/h.ts"]), then hook("h", ["out/h.ts"]); then first {commit: HEAD, diffstat {files: 1, insertions: 1, deletions: 0}} with the HEAD message "morph h: out/h.ts\n\nMorph-Card: h\nMorph-Model: stub\nMorph-Acceptance-Exit: 0"; second null and HEAD unchanged
4. given a repo whose committed .gitignore holds "out/\n"; hook = makeCommitHook(root, "m2", env); out/g.ts written "y\n"; when hook("g", ["out/g.ts"]); then {commit: HEAD, diffstat {files: 1, insertions: 1, deletions: 0}}, no throw; `git show --name-only --format= HEAD` reads "out/g.ts"; the message "morph g: out/g.ts\n\nMorph-Card: g\nMorph-Model: m2\nMorph-Acceptance-Exit: 0"

## Function Run Acceptance

Executes the card's acceptance command from the repo root.

Behaviour: runAcceptance(command, root, {env, timeoutMs}) spawns /bin/sh -c with cwd = root, env = the given env minus every key whose upper-cased name starts with MORPH_PROCESSOR_ or ends in _KEY or _TOKEN (no key reaches a model-written test), with NO_COLOR=1 and CI=1 laid over it (nothing else; the caller's object is not changed), detached in its own process group; stdout and stderr merged in write order. timeoutMs defaults to 300000: on expiry the whole process group is killed, so no child outlives the call, and the result is exit null, timedOut true, the output so far kept with the line "acceptance timed out after <ms> ms" appended. The log is clipped by clipLog: over 4000 chars it keeps the first 1500 and the last 1500 chars and, between them, a marker and every middle line that looks like a diagnosis (FAIL, Error, assert, expected), within 800 chars. Returns Acceptance Result.

Steps:
- produces: Acceptance Result

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given command `echo out; echo err >&2; exit 3`, env {PATH: "/usr/bin:/bin"}; when run; then {exit: 3, log: "out\nerr\n", timedOut: false}

3. given command `echo started; sleep 30 & echo $! > sleep.pid; wait`, env {PATH: "/usr/bin:/bin"}, timeoutMs 200; when run; then {exit: null, timedOut: true, log: "started\nacceptance timed out after 200 ms\n"}, returned in under 2000 ms; the sleep whose pid is in root/sleep.pid is gone (no /proc/<pid>, or its state is Z): the process group was killed, no orphan

## Function Run Deck

Generations in order, the budget at each boundary, retries per card (2) capped per generation, a carried-over retry before its dependants, a fault caught, the Run Report.

Behaviour: runDeck(input, deps) runs input.deck generation by generation in the order of layerGenerations(input.deck). At each generation boundary: deps.now() >= input.budget.deadline → every not-yet-done card of this and later generations becomes {status "budget-exceeded", reason "deadline"}; cardsProcessed >= input.budget.maxCards → reason "maxCards <maxCards>". Otherwise, when a not-yet-done card of the generation has a dependsOn id whose outcome is "failed" with retries left, the retry loop below runs FIRST (same cap, same deadline check), so a dependency written by a carried-over retry unblocks it; then it resolves the runnable cards (resolveRunnable, the statuses so far), records the skipped, runs processGeneration on the runnable, accumulates usage and request rows, keeps each failed card's Retry Context (by original id; a later round's replaces an earlier one), adds the runnable count to cardsProcessed. Retries: 2 per card, in whichever generation it runs; input.budget.maxRetryBatches caps the retry batches of ONE generation (retryBatches starts at 0 at each): while some failed card has been retried fewer than 2 times and retryBatches < maxRetryBatches, a retry batch runs (retryBatches += 1) for all such cards (an earlier generation's included), unless deps.now() >= the deadline, checked before each batch: then each such card becomes its outcome with status "budget-exceeded", reason "deadline", and no batch runs. A batch: buildRetry(original card, retryNumber, the latest Retry Context's acceptanceOutput, its previousDiff) each, processGeneration on them; a written retry updates the card's outcome (status "written", its commit, attempts = retry number + 1), every attempt's log appended to earlierFailures. The Run Report: runId, completedAt = deps.now(), branch = input.branch, processor = deps.config.id, generations = the count, outcomes in deck order, usageTotals {inputTokens, outputTokens summed; cost the sum of reported costs, null when none; requests = the usage row count}, requests = every Request Usage row of the run in send order. Returns {report, outcomes}. deps reach every processGeneration call as given (onVariant sees the retries). It writes and commits nothing. It never rejects: a value thrown inside the run (the commit hook, an answer write) stops it; every card with no outcome yet becomes {status "skipped", reason "fault", attempts 0, winningVariant null, acceptanceLog "", earlierFailures [], commit null, diffstat null} (the usage of the call in flight is lost) and the report's last key is fault = the Error's message (String(value) otherwise); no fault, no key.

- calls: Resolve Runnable

Requirements:
- Strict TypeScript: tsconfig strict, ESM, no `any`; every module compiles with tsc --noEmit.
- One Document Out: Every command prints exactly one JSON document on stdout and nothing else; the human log goes to stderr.
- Deterministic Core: cards and compiler give byte-identical results for the same inputs: no clock, no randomness, no environment reads. acceptance is bound only in its pure parts (Snapshot Targets, Build Attempt Diff): Run Acceptance spawns a shell and its only timer is the child's timeout; env and the timeout are parameters, never process.env (06.10, P3). processor reads the environment only in Read Registry; Assemble Request, Read Response, Stub Answer, Assemble Batch and Read Batch are pure of clock and network; the transport and its sleep are parameters of Send Generation and Send Batch (P4, P11). git spawns only in Run Git, synchronously, with the child's environment given whole as a parameter; it reads no process.env and no clock of its own (P6). cli touches the process only in its entry src/cli.ts: the environment, the working directory, the clock and the output streams reach main() as parameters, and the environment reaches the processor only through Read Registry (P7). language is pure data and pure functions: no clock, no environment, no file system, no child process; node:path is its only Node module; its shell lines are text (P8). contour reads no file, no clock and no environment: it parses the text it is given; the package yaml is imported in Parse Document alone (P9). planner reads no file, no clock and no environment: the cli reads the record and the map and passes which files exist as a function; node:path is its only Node module (P10a). builder reads no file, no clock and no environment: the caller passes the checks, the cards, the profile and the texts of the guard, the locator and the probes; node:path is its only Node module (P10b).

- Frozen Tree During Run: while a run is in flight no file outside the cards' targets and .morph/ changes; a changed declared input discards the answer unread.
